title: Cisco CCNP Security Study Guide
description: CCNP Security is Cisco's network-security engineering certification — the SCOR core plus one concentration, covering firewalls, identity (ISE), VPN/SSE, and from v2.0, AI-era security. Read this before anything else: 2026 is a transition year. SCOR v1.1's last test day is August 26, 2026; v2.0 launches August 27 — and three concentration exams retire outright on the same date.
audience: Network engineers pivoting into security engineering — people who build and run Cisco Secure Firewall, ISE/NAC, and VPN/SSE estates. Explicitly NOT a SOC analyst cert: if your target is alert triage, incident response, and threat hunting, that's Cisco's separate CCNP Cybersecurity (the renamed CyberOps Professional). Confusing these two wastes a year.
why_get_it: It's consistently cited as the highest-paying CCNP track, and the reason is scarcity of the profile: engineers who genuinely know both enterprise networking and the Cisco security stack — Secure Firewall (FTD/FMC), ISE, secure connectivity — are rare and expensive. Every exam passed earns a standalone Specialist credential along the way, and SCOR doubles as the CCIE Security qualifying exam. The honest scope note: this is a Cisco-product expert path, and its value tracks your employer's Cisco footprint. In Palo Alto or Fortinet shops it buys less; pair it with Security+ or CISSP for the vendor-neutral HR-filter layer.
when_to_get_it: After CCNA-level networking plus real exposure to firewalls, VPNs, and identity concepts — SCOR will bury pure-theory candidates. And in 2026, timing IS the strategy: if you're mid-study on v1.1 material (or targeting SESA, SWSA, or SVPN — all three retire), you must test by August 26, 2026. Starting fresh? Study straight to the v2.0/v1.2 blueprints and expect official training to lag — Cisco ships partial v2.0 training in Q3 2026, full in Q4. Both windows are legitimate choices — drifting across the boundary mid-prep is the expensive mistake.
salary_note: Placement trackers consistently call CCNP Security the highest-paying CCNP: ZipRecruiter-class data shows ~$150K averages for tagged roles (with the usual title-skew caveats), PayScale pegs cert-holder medians nearer $113K. The realistic band is $110–155K, with federal/cleared roles and Fortune-500 firewall+ISE work at the top. All third-party estimates — no official Cisco salary data exists.
exam_format: Two proctored exams at Pearson VUE (test center or OnVUE): the SCOR core (multiple-choice, drag-and-drop, performance-based; count and passing score not published) plus one concentration. Results in ~48 hours. No lab exam at CCNP level.

exam_structure.note: v1.1 last test day Aug 26, 2026; v2.0 live Aug 27 (adds AI/LLM security, Zero Trust/SSE/SASE, post-quantum crypto). Also the CCIE Security qualifying exam. Earns Specialist – Security Core.

exam_structure.note: The identity/NAC lane — ISE expertise is among the most billable Cisco skills. v1.2 (ISE 3.4/3.5) from Aug 27, 2026.

exam_structure.name: Designing and Implementing Secure Cloud Access for Users and Endpoints
exam_structure.note: Major v2.0 rewrite Aug 27, 2026: multicloud, ZTNA, AI guardrails.

exam_structure.name: SESA (email), SWSA (web), SVPN (VPN)
exam_structure.note: All three retire Aug 26, 2026 with no replacements. Only start one if you can test before that date.

recertification_note: 3-year cycle, 80 CE credits — the unified ledger: core exam re-pass = 80 CE, concentrations = 40 each, training CE from Cisco U counts too, excess rolls over. Two concentrations across a cycle keeps you certified without re-facing SCOR.

study_steps.title: Pick your side of August 26, 2026 — first, before anything
study_steps.description: The single most important decision: test v1.1 by Aug 26 (mature study materials, but a deadline), or start clean on v2.0 from Aug 27 (current content — AI security, SSE, PQC — but official training arrives in waves, Q3–Q4 2026). Mid-study drift across that boundary is the expensive mistake. If SESA/SWSA/SVPN was your concentration plan, the deadline is absolute — they retire with no replacements.

study_steps.title: Confirm this is your track — not CCNP Cybersecurity
study_steps.description: Thirty seconds that saves a year: CCNP Security = build and run the security infrastructure (firewalls, ISE, VPN/SSE). CCNP Cybersecurity (renamed CyberOps Professional) = SOC operations, forensics, threat hunting. Different careers, different exams. If your target is analyst work, stop here and switch guides.

study_steps.title: Choose the concentration by your job market
study_steps.description: SNCF (firewalls) has the most postings behind it; SISE (ISE/identity) is the most billable specialty; SCAZT covers the cloud/ZTNA direction the industry is moving; SDSI suits architecture-leaning engineers. Pick before starting SCOR so your lab time compounds.

study_steps.title: Lab on DevNet sandboxes — the stack is unaffordable otherwise
study_steps.description: Nobody home-labs FMC, ISE, and the content stack legally on a budget. Cisco's free DevNet sandboxes carry reservable ISE and Secure Firewall instances — the realistic hands-on route. Add dcloud.cisco.com guided demos with a free account, and Katherine McNamara's free ISE labs at network-node.com (the unofficial SISE bible — verify version coverage against ISE 3.4/3.5 for v1.2).

study_steps.title: Build the SCOR spine from the OCG plus blueprint deltas
study_steps.description: Omar Santos's SCOR Official Cert Guide is the standard text — but it targets v1.1, and no v2.0 edition exists at the changeover. If you're on the v2.0 side, study the book for the durable 70% and fill AI-security, SSE/SASE, and post-quantum topics straight from the blueprint and Cisco U content as it lands.

study_steps.title: Calibrate with Boson before burning $400
study_steps.description: Boson's SCOR ExSim is the most exam-realistic practice available and the best predictor of readiness. Consistent mid-80s = book it. Version-check the bank against your chosen blueprint side.

study_steps.title: Sit SCOR, bank two doors at once
study_steps.description: Passing earns Specialist – Security Core immediately and qualifies you for the CCIE Security lab. 120 minutes, results in ~48 hours.

study_steps.title: Close out the concentration while the core is fresh
study_steps.description: 90 minutes, $300. SNCF and SISE reward the sandbox hours you already logged; SDSI leans design-brain over lab-brain. Passing completes CCNP Security and banks 40 CE toward the next cycle.

study_steps.title: Add the vendor-neutral layer for HR
study_steps.description: The blunt market truth: many security-manager and government postings filter on Security+ or CISSP regardless of how deep your Cisco skills run. CCNP Security proves you can build it; pair it with the neutral credential that gets the resume opened. Our Security+ and CISSP guides cover both.

study_steps.title: Keep current the cheap way
study_steps.description: 80 CE per 3 years: one concentration re-pass (40) plus free Cisco U 'Rev Up' promos usually covers it. Watch for time-boxed free official courses too — Cisco periodically gives away full concentration prep worth 40+ CE.

faq.question: What's this August 2026 deadline everyone mentions?
faq.answer: Cisco's biggest security-track transition in years: SCOR v1.1, SNCF v1.1, SISE v1.1, and SCAZT v1.0 all have a last test date of August 26, 2026, with v2.0/v1.2 versions launching August 27 — and three concentrations (SESA email, SWSA web, SVPN) retire outright that day with no replacements. Decide which side of the boundary you're on before you start studying, not mid-way.

faq.question: CCNP Security or CCNP Cybersecurity — aren't they the same thing?
faq.answer: No, and the naming genuinely trips people. CCNP Security (SCOR + concentration) is security ENGINEERING: you build and operate firewalls, ISE, VPN/SSE. CCNP Cybersecurity — the renamed CyberOps Professional (CBRCOR core + forensics or threat-hunting concentration) — is security OPERATIONS: SOC work, incident response, hunting. Pick by which chair you want: builder or defender-analyst.

faq.question: Which concentration should I pick?
faq.answer: SNCF (firewalls) for the most job postings; SISE (ISE/identity) for the most billable specialty; SCAZT for the ZTNA/cloud direction; SDSI for design-leaning engineers. Do not start SESA, SWSA, or SVPN unless you can test before August 26, 2026 — they retire with no successors.

faq.question: Is CCNP Security worth it outside Cisco shops?
faq.answer: Less — be honest with yourself here. This is a Cisco-product expert path; its market value tracks your employer's (or target employers') Cisco security footprint. In Palo Alto or Fortinet estates, it buys goodwill but not mastery-fit. Vendor-neutral trajectory (CISO-track, architecture)? CISSP plus this or instead of this. Pure Cisco shop? Few certs pay better.

faq.question: What does SCOR v2.0 actually add?
faq.answer: The 2026 threat landscape, essentially: AI/LLM security vulnerabilities, Zero Trust and SSE/SASE as first-class architecture, Splunk telemetry, eBPF workload protection, and post-quantum cryptography awareness. It's a genuinely more current exam — the trade-off is that official training lands in waves (partial Q3, full Q4 2026) and third-party material will lag into 2027.

faq.question: Does SCOR count toward CCIE Security?
faq.answer: Yes — SCOR is simultaneously the CCNP Security core and the CCIE Security qualifying exam. Pass it and you're eligible to book the 8-hour lab. Same efficient pattern as the Enterprise track: the professional cert's core is the expert cert's entry ticket.

faq.question: How do I keep it current without re-taking SCOR?
faq.answer: 80 CE credits per 3-year cycle, and concentrations pay 40 each — so one additional concentration per cycle plus modest Cisco U coursework keeps you certified indefinitely. Watch for Cisco's periodic free official courses; they've given away full concentration prep worth 40+ CE before.
